You are a professional biblical lexicographer fluent in Spanish. Translate the following English lexicon entry into Spanish.

Lemma: H7999b

ENGLISH GLOSSES TO TRANSLATE:
  Terse gloss: "To be at peace, make peace, fulfill, or be wholly devoted; from the root שׁלם expressing completeness, wholeness, and covenant harmony."
  Readable gloss: "This denominative verb draws on the rich semantic field of שׁלם — wholeness, completeness, peace. In its Hifil form, it most often means to make peace with another party, as when the Gibeonites made peace with Israel (Josh 10:1, 4) or when Jehoshaphat was at peace with the king of Israel (1 Kgs 22:44). The Qal conveys a stative sense of being at peace or in covenant friendship, as in Job 22:21 ('be at peace with him') and Psalm 7:4 ('the one at peace with me'). A distinct Hifil nuance appears in Isaiah 44:26, where God 'fulfills' or brings to completion the word of his servant. The Pual participle in Isaiah 42:19 describes one who is devoted or wholehearted — the 'perfected one.' Spanish 'pacíficas' and 'cumple' neatly distinguish the peace and fulfillment senses."

SENSES:
  Sense 1: "Hifil/Hofal: make peace"
    Enriched: Hifil and Hofal: to make peace, establish a covenant of peace, or have peace made. This is the dominant sense, covering military and political contexts such as Joshua 10:1 and 11:19, where Canaanite cities make peace with Israel. Deuteronomy 20:12 provides the negative case: a city that does not make peace. Spanish 'hizo paz' and 'hicieron paz' reflect the treaty-making character directly.
    Existing Spanish translations: E-hizo-paz, e-hicieron-paz, hace-estar-en-paz, hace-paz, harán-paz, hicieron-paz, hizo-paz
  Sense 2: "Qal: be at peace"
    Enriched: Qal stative and participial: to be at peace, to be in a state of peaceful covenant relationship. In Job 22:21, Eliphaz urges Job to 'be at peace' with God and receive good; in Psalm 7:4 David speaks of 'the one at peace with me,' his ally. The passive participle in 2 Samuel 20:19 describes the 'peaceable' faithful of Israel. Spanish 'pacíficas' captures the relational quality of this peace.
    Existing Spanish translations: al-que-estaba-en-paz-conmigo, de-las-pacíficas, y-ten-paz;
  Sense 3: "Hifil: fulfill, complete"
    Enriched: Hifil in a completive sense: to fulfill, accomplish, or bring to completion. Distinct from peace-making, this reflects the root meaning of wholeness or finishing. In Isaiah 44:26, God 'fulfills' (יַשְׁלִים) the word of his servant and completes the counsel of his messengers. Spanish 'cumple' precisely renders this fulfillment nuance.
    Existing Spanish translations: cumple
  Sense 4: "Pual: devoted, wholehearted"
    Enriched: Pual passive participle: devoted, wholehearted, one who has been made whole or complete. In Isaiah 42:19, the LORD's servant is called מְשֻׁלָּם — the 'perfected' or 'devoted one.' Spanish 'el perfecto' highlights the completeness rather than peace, and scholarly debate on this form (some reading 'their ruler' with the LXX) underscores the interpretive richness of this rare usage.
    Existing Spanish translations: como-el-perfecto
